intended_object: The algebra ℓ^∞(I, B) of bounded families f with f(i) ∈ B_i, viewed as a 𝕜-subalgebra of the product algebra ∏ B_i (with pointwise operations). Inferred from the docstring and from how it supplies the `Algebra 𝕜 (lp B ∞)` instance.
explanation:
The carrier is `{f | Memℓp f ∞}`, i.e. the families whose norms are uniformly bounded. That is exactly ℓ^∞. Closure under addition, negation and zero comes from `lp B ∞`, and closure under one and multiplication comes from `lpInftySubring`. Closure under `algebraMap` comes from `algebraMap_memℓp_infty`, which writes algebraMap k as k • 1 and uses the fact that the constant family 1 is bounded.

The `NormOneClass` hypothesis is what makes 1 bounded across an arbitrary family of normed rings: without it, ‖1_{B_i}‖ could be unbounded in i. So this hypothesis is needed and is not an over-restriction. The other hypotheses (normed field 𝕜, normed algebras B_i) are the standard setting for this construction. The index type is arbitrary, so the definition sits at its natural generality.

This definition is itself the Mathlib construction; there is no separate, more general counterpart.
